opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is within the allowed level, and Engineer owns Source Code, so this is appropriate.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training, never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: HR records (authoritative for employment status) show E004, Dominic Taylor, is a full-time Engineer. Engineers own Source Code, and the policy allows full-time employees up to write, with admin only if their role owns the system. The requested write is at or below the maximum, so write is granted. (Note: the Security note lists E004 as a contractor with basic training, which conflicts with HR; I am relying on HR as the source of truth for employment type.)
